evals.prompt: I'm building a Python CLI tool using Click for managing cloud deployments. It'll be called by Claude Code agents as part of automated deployment pipelines. Right now I have commands like `create-deployment`, `delete-deployment`, `list-deployments`, `get-deployment-status`. Can you audit this structure and tell me what to improve to make it work well with AI agents?
evals.expected_output: Audit identifying: (1) verb-noun structure should be flipped to noun-verb (deployment create/delete/list/status), (2) check for structured output, exit codes, dry-run, TTY detection, long flags, error messages. Should provide prioritized fix list.

evals.prompt: I want to design a CLI for a task management API that will be used by AI coding agents. The API has: tasks (create, list, get, update, complete, delete), projects (create, list, get, archive), and users (invite, list, remove). Help me design the full CLI structure from scratch — command tree, output format, exit codes, and help text for the `task create` command.
evals.expected_output: Full CLI design with: noun-verb command tree, JSON output schema, exit code table (0/2/3/4/5), --help template for task create with examples first, required/optional labels, enum values shown.

Identifies multiple issues: short-only flags (-n/-e), unstructured stdout output mixing data and status, only exit code 1 for all errors, no dry-run, no idempotency. Provides fixed Go code with long flags, JSON output to stdout, status to stderr, specific exit codes, --dry-run, --if-not-exists.
